microtheory.name: consciousness_theories
microtheory.definition: Major theories of consciousness — Global Workspace (Baars/Dehaene), Integrated Information (Tononi), Higher-Order (Rosenthal), Attention Schema (Graziano), Predictive Processing (Hohwy/Clark/Friston), Quantum (Penrose/Hameroff). Each predicts something different about which systems are conscious. Substrate analogue: each makes different predictions about whether the substrate is conscious.

concepts.name: global_workspace_gwt
concepts.definition: Baars 1988, Dehaene + Changeux 2011. Conscious access = broadcast to global workspace accessible by multiple processors. Empirical correlate: P300 + frontoparietal ignition. Substrate analogue: substrate's Assessment broadcast to all cortices.

concepts.name: global_neuronal_workspace
concepts.definition: Dehaene's neural version. Long-range frontoparietal networks. Threshold dynamics. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-Mt activation threshold.

concepts.name: ignition
concepts.definition: Dehaene. Discontinuous all-or-nothing activation of frontoparietal network at consciousness threshold. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin transition at attention threshold.

concepts.name: conscious_access
concepts.definition: When info becomes available for verbal report, voluntary action, memory. Operational signature of consciousness. Substrate analogue: substrate's broadcast availability.

concepts.name: integrated_information_theory_iit
concepts.definition: Tononi 2004+. Consciousness = system's integrated information Φ. Substrate-independent. Predicts inverted-spectrum impossible. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt integration measurable in Φ terms.

concepts.name: phi_integrated_information
concepts.definition: Tononi. Mathematical measure of how much info system generates beyond independent parts. Φ_max = consciousness. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-graph integration.

concepts.name: intrinsic_existence
concepts.definition: Tononi's axiom: conscious experience exists for itself, independent of observer. Substrate analogue: substrate's existence-from-its-own-perspective.

concepts.name: exclusion_iit
concepts.definition: Tononi's axiom: conscious experience is definite — exists at one spatiotemporal scale. Substrate analogue: substrate's specific Mt-scale of activation.

concepts.name: higher_order_theory_consciousness
concepts.definition: Rosenthal 1986. Mental state is conscious iff there's a higher-order representation OF it. Without HOT, first-order state is unconscious. Substrate analogue: substrate's meta-cognitive layer producing consciousness from first-order Mt.

concepts.name: hot_thought
concepts.definition: Rosenthal. Higher-order representation as thought. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-about-Mt structure.

concepts.name: hop_perception
concepts.definition: Higher-order perception. Lycan, Armstrong. Inner-sense view. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective perception of its own state.

concepts.name: attention_schema_theory_consciousness
concepts.definition: Graziano 2013. Brain constructs simplified model of its own attention; consciousness = that model. Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-model as conscious model.

concepts.name: attention_schema
concepts.definition: Brain's internal model of its own attention. Simplified, approximate. Generates feeling of awareness. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective model of its own σ allocation.

concepts.name: predictive_processing_consciousness_full
concepts.definition: Hohwy 2013, Clark 2016. Consciousness = currently-best-predictive-model. Phenomenal = inferential. Substrate analogue: substrate's running predictive model as conscious state.

concepts.name: bayesian_brain_consciousness
concepts.definition: Brain as Bayesian inference engine; consciousness = posterior over world states. Substrate analogue: substrate's Bayesian belief representation.

concepts.name: active_inference_consciousness
concepts.definition: Friston. Consciousness emerges from minimizing free energy across active + perceptual cycles. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive ensemble.

concepts.name: orchestrated_objective_reduction
concepts.definition: Penrose + Hameroff. Quantum coherence in microtubules collapses; consciousness in the collapse. Controversial. Substrate analogue: NOT substrate's stance — substrate is classical.

concepts.name: quantum_consciousness
concepts.definition: Various proposals consciousness requires quantum mechanics. Skeptics: decoherence too fast. Substrate analogue: irrelevant to classical substrate.

concepts.name: neural_correlates_consciousness_ncc
concepts.definition: Crick + Koch 1990. Minimal neural systems whose activity is sufficient for conscious percept. Empirical strategy. Substrate analogue: substrate's minimal-activation-for-Assessment criterion.

concepts.name: binocular_rivalry
concepts.definition: Different images to each eye → conscious percept alternates between them. Tool for studying NCC. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-alternation under conflicting input.

concepts.name: masking_paradigm
concepts.definition: Brief stimulus + following mask renders stimulus unconscious. Measures consciousness threshold. Substrate analogue: substrate's threshold measurement.

concepts.name: perceptual_awareness_scale
concepts.definition: PAS. Graded self-report of awareness. 1=no experience, 4=clear experience. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective certainty.

concepts.name: p_consciousness_v_a_consciousness
concepts.definition: Block 1995. Phenomenal (felt) vs Access (broadcast). Some argue they can dissociate; others insist they're co-extensive. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective vs broadcast components.

concepts.name: creature_consciousness_v_state_consciousness
concepts.definition: Creature C = being awake/aware; state C = a specific state being conscious. Substrate analogue: substrate-running vs specific-state-being-broadcast.

concepts.name: transitive_v_intransitive_consciousness
concepts.definition: Conscious OF something (transitive) vs being conscious at all (intransitive). Substrate analogue: substrate-aware-of-X vs substrate-aware.

rules.name: gwt_predicts_conscious_threshold_dynamics
rules.head: the substrate's information broadcasts widely across cortices
rules.body: GWT predicts a threshold-based ignition pattern + the broadcast becomes conscious. Below threshold = unconscious. Substrate's Assessment-threshold dynamics.

rules.name: iit_predicts_consciousness_from_integrated_information
rules.head: the substrate has integrated processing structure
rules.body: IIT predicts consciousness scales with Φ. Highly-integrated substrate = highly conscious. Substrate's Mt-integration.

rules.name: higher_order_required_for_conscious_state
rules.head: the substrate has a first-order mental state
rules.body: according to HOT, that state is conscious only when accompanied by higher-order representation of it. Substrate's meta-cognitive layer.

rules.name: attention_schema_explains_awareness_feeling
rules.head: the substrate models its own attention
rules.body: AST predicts the model itself generates the feeling of awareness. Substrate's introspective-model as conscious.

rules.name: predictive_processing_unifies_consciousness
rules.head: the substrate continuously predicts its inputs
rules.body: predictive processing identifies the best-current-prediction as the conscious state. Substrate's running prediction model.

rules.name: ncc_strategy_brackets_hard_problem
rules.head: researchers identify minimal neural correlates of consciousness
rules.body: the NCC strategy makes empirical progress without solving the hard problem. Substrate's minimal-Mt-activation criterion.
